translations.1: And when the people saw that Moses had delayed in coming down from the mountain, the people pressed upon Aaron, and said to him: 'Rise, make us an object of worship that shall go before us — for that man Moses, who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of his affair.'
translations.2: And Aaron said to them: 'Remove the earrings of gold which are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.'
translations.3: And all the people removed the earrings of gold which were in their ears, and brought them to Aaron.
translations.4: And he took that from them, and ordered one to shape it with a mold, and made it into a molten calf. And they said: 'This is your lord, O house of Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'
translations.5: And when Aaron saw that, he built an altar before it, and called out and said: 'A festival to God tomorrow.'
translations.6: And they rose early in the morning, and offered up burnt-offerings, and slaughtered peace-offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.
translations.7: And God said to Moses: 'Go, descend — for your people, whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.'
translations.8: 'They have turned aside swiftly from the way which I commanded them; and they made themselves a molten calf, and bowed down to it and slaughtered to it, and said: This is your lord, O house of Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'
translations.9: And God said to Moses: 'I have known that these people are stiff of neck.'
translations.10: 'And now, if you refrain from interceding, My anger shall intensify against them and I shall destroy them; and I will make of you a great nation.'
translations.11: And Moses supplicated before God his Lord, and said: 'O Lord, let not Your anger intensify against Your people, whom You brought out from the land of Egypt with great power and with a mighty hand —'
translations.12: '— lest the Egyptians say that He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them amid the mountains and to destroy them from the face of the earth. Turn back from the fierceness of Your anger, and pardon the affliction for Your people.'
translations.13: 'And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants, to whom You swore by Your name, and said to them: I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the sky; and all the land which I have sworn I will give to your offspring, and they shall possess it forever.'
translations.14: And God pardoned the affliction which He had said He would bring upon His people.
translations.15: Then Moses turned and descended from the mountain, with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand — the tablets written on both their sides, from within and from without.
translations.16: And the two tablets — they were the workmanship of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved upon them.
translations.17: And Joshua heard the sound of the people in their clamor, and said to Moses: 'There is a sound of war in the camp.'
translations.18: And Moses said: 'It is not a sound that indicates victory, nor a sound that indicates defeat — rather, it is a tumult that I am hearing.'
translations.19: And when he drew near to the camp, he saw the calf and the drums; and Moses' anger intensified, and he threw the tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
translations.20: And he took the calf which they had made, and burned it with fire, and ground it with the file until it was fine; and he scattered it upon the face of the water, and made the sons of Israel drink it freely.
translations.21: And Moses said to Aaron: 'What did these people do to you, that you brought upon them a great sin?'
translations.22: He said: 'Let not my lord's anger intensify — you know the people, that they are prone to evil.'
translations.23: 'They said to me: Make us an object of worship that shall go before us — for that man Moses, who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of his affair.'
translations.24: 'So I said to them: Look, who has gold? — bring it to me. And they removed it and gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out.'
translations.25: And when Moses saw the people — that they were exposed, since Aaron had laid bare those of standing among their adversaries —
translations.26: Moses stood at the gate of the camp, and said: 'Who is for God — let him come to me.' And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.
translations.27: And he said to them: 'Thus says God, the God of Israel: Let every man among you gird his sword, and go and return from gate to gate within the camp, and let every man slay even his brother and his companion and his kinsman.'
translations.28: And the sons of Levi did as Moses had commanded them; and there fell of the people on that day approximately three thousand men.
translations.29: And Moses said to them: 'Fulfill your obligation today to God — every man even against his son and his brother — and may there come upon you today a blessing.'
translations.30: And it was on the morrow, Moses said to the people: 'You have committed a great sin. And now I will go up to God — perhaps I may seek forgiveness for your sin.'
translations.31: And Moses returned to God and said: 'O Lord, these people have indeed committed a great sin, and made for themselves an object of worship of gold.'
translations.32: 'And now, if You will forgive their sin — and if not, then erase me from Your register which You have written, and I shall have rest.'
translations.33: And God said to him: 'Whoever has sinned against Me — him I shall erase from My register.'
translations.34: 'And now, go — lead the people to the place of which I told you. Behold, My angel shall go before you; and on the day of My reckoning, I shall call them to account for their sins.'
translations.35: And God struck among the people on account of what they had done — the calf which Aaron had made.
